candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record shows the classic MEN2A triad: markedly elevated calcitonin/CEA (MTC), massively elevated urinary metanephrines (pheochromocytoma), and elevated intact PTH with normal calcium (early/normocalcemic hyperparathyroidism). The candidate correctly names MEN2 with MTC and pheochromocytoma but omits the critical 2A subtype designation, leaving open the possibility of MEN2B (which lacks hyperparathyroidism and has a distinct phenotype). The reference requires MEN2A specifically.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies MEN2 with MTC and pheochromocytoma but does not specify the subtype (2A vs 2B); elevated PTH and the submental cystic lesion (possibly a parathyroid adenoma or thyroglossal duct cyst) are consistent with MEN2A, which requires hyperparathyroidism as the distinguishing third component over MEN2B

case_quality_flags: Submental midline lesion with calcifications is unexplained by MEN2A alone; differential includes thyroglossal duct cyst or ectopic parathyroid adenoma
Normal serum calcium despite elevated PTH may indicate early/normocalcemic primary hyperparathyroidism consistent with MEN2A
No family history reported but de novo MEN2A (RET mutation) is possible
